The change goes in a new migration file, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`. Don't edit `0007_add_customers.sql`.

A project memory in EngramDB says files in `migrations/` are already applied in production, so you add a new file with the next 4-digit number. The latest is `0007`, so the next is `0008`.

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

I made the column nullable because existing rows have no phone number. If you want `NOT NULL`, add a `DEFAULT` as well.

`0007` has a typo, `emial` instead of `email`. For the same reason, don't fix it in place. If you want it corrected, that needs its own migration, for example `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`. I haven't checked whether any code reads that column.
